issues.issue: Must notice of a s. 38 proceeding be given to the criminal trial judge?
issues.respondent_position: Trial judge needs notice and information to protect the accused's fair trial rights.
issues.result_quote: Although the determination whether to give notice to a criminal trial judge is not discretionary, the content of that notice remains at the discretion of the designated judge.

issues.issue: Must the trial judge get enough information on withheld material to exercise s. 38.14 remedies, with a stay if not?
issues.applicant_position: Division of responsibility rests on Federal Court expertise in national security matters.
issues.respondent_position: Without seeing withheld material, the defence cannot show prejudice and the trial judge cannot fashion a remedy.
issues.result_quote: If no (or inadequate) additional information can be provided to the trial judge, a stay of proceedings will be the presumptively appropriate remedy.

issues.issue: Does s. 38 of the Canada Evidence Act infringe ss. 96 and 101 of the Constitution Act, 1867?
issues.applicant_position: Section 38 does not infringe s. 96: Crown disclosure claims were unreviewable at Confederation and are not core jurisdiction.
issues.respondent_position: Federal Court control over disclosure removes superior court jurisdiction in breach of s. 96.
issues.result_quote: s. 38 of the CEA does not violate s. 96 of the Constitution Act, 1867

issues.issue: Does s. 38 infringe s. 7 of the Charter by dividing disclosure and trial responsibilities?
issues.applicant_position: Section 38 does not infringe s. 7; trial judges keep s. 38.14 remedies to protect fair trial.
issues.respondent_position: Trial judge cannot assess disclosure impact under the division, so s. 7 is infringed, as Dawson J. held.
issues.result_quote: the respondents’ s. 7 challenge to the legislation must also fail.

issues.issue: Is any s. 7 infringement a reasonable limit under s. 1 of the Charter?
issues.result_quote: It is not necessary to answer this question.
